text:
maria_cs: FYI - Ignite onboarding hitting transient 429s when their serverless warmers scale up. They reported it started when they increased parallel warm invocations from ~10 -> ~120. Pattern looks like a burst of short-lived auth requests paired with chat calls.

maria_cs: customer logs pasted: 
```
2026-03-02T09:21:10Z INFO id=xyz01 POST /v1/chat 200 time=110ms
2026-03-02T09:21:10Z WARN id=xyz02 POST /v1/chat 429 time=22ms x-rate-limit-reset=15
2026-03-02T09:21:11Z WARN id=xyz03 POST /v1/chat 429 time=20ms x-rate-limit-remaining=0
```

maria_cs: they said their flow calls an internal auth endpoint to mint short-lived tokens for each invocation (ttl=30s) and they don't persist sockets between invocations. using python lambda with requests per event.

nina_se: thanks. ephemeral-token-per-invocation + no socket reuse = classic preflight stampede. ask them for the auth response body (does it return ttl) and their client snippet. prefer a minimal repro if they can run locally.

maria_cs: they returned the auth payload: `{"access":"...", "expires_in": 30}`. client snippet: 
```python
# handler.py
token = requests.post('https://auth.ignite.local/get').json()['access']
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'}, json=payload)
```

dan_engineer: two quick asks: 1) cache token in the runtime/process for (expires_in - 5s) 2) enable HTTP keep-alive / connection pooling (persistent sessions) 3) add randomized jitter on cold-start warmers so they don't all request at once.

dan_engineer: sample Python patch: 
```python
# tiny token cache + session
import time, requests
_session = requests.Session()
_cache = { 'token': None, 'exp': 0 }

def get_token():
    if time.time() < _cache['exp'] - 5:
        return _cache['token']
    r = requests.post('https://auth.ignite.local/get')
    data = r.json()
    _cache['token'] = data['access']
    _cache['exp'] = time.time() + data['expires_in']
    return _cache['token']

# then use _session.post(..., headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {get_token()}"})
```

tyler_support: I'll ask them to roll that patch as a 5-10% canary in prod. also recommend they reduce their lambda concurrency burst and add a warm-up splay: `sleep(random.uniform(0, 1.5))` on init.

maria_cs: customer applied the cache + session in staging — 429s dropped from 6.5% -> 0.4% within 10m. good signal.

nina_se: great. on our side, ops can open a 20-min grace window lowering early hard-fail 429 enforcement for that tenant while they ramp. low risk if we gate by a header we detect (e.g., `x-client-token-cache: true`).

ops_bot: mitigation created: #CS-4902 owner=nina_se expires=20m playbook=token-cache-grace


dan_engineer: extra SDK options to pass to Ignite if they adopt our SDK: `session_pool=True`, `max_connections_per_host=32`, and `token_cache=True`. also add a small client-side retry-on-429 with exponential backoff and jitter (don't hammer immediately).

maria_cs: customer's product team asked if we can emit a telemetry header indicating the gateway saw many auth validations in a short window. they'd use that to surface risk in their SRE dashboards.

dan_engineer: we can prototype `x-token-pressure: hot` when we detect >50 auth checks/min from a single tenant origin. small feature flag task. I'll file it.

tyler_support: next steps for customer: 1) keep canary at 10% for 20m 2) if 429s < 1% and latency stable, ramp to 100% over 30m 3) add token-cache to their onboarding checklist + include TTL check. we'll monitor via console metrics and ask CS to post updates here.

maria_cs: logging their renewal note: customer was worried this would be a long-term reliability risk. fixing this during onboarding is important for renewal confidence. captured in SDR notes.

nina_se: internal follow-up: add a unit/integration test that simulates 150 concurrent functions fetching fresh tokens and hitting /v1/chat to ensure our backpressure/soft-fail behavior works. also update the public KB entry about ephemeral tokens anti-pattern and include code samples for node/python.

maria_cs: prod canary started — initial 10% rollout looks good. will update after 30m. :thumbsup:

ops_bot: #CS-4902 updated status=monitoring owner=tyler_support

maria_cs: 35m update: canary healthy, 429s at baseline, customer proceeded to 100% ramp. they added token-cache to their deploy checklist. closing this thread in 24h if no regressions. thanks everyone! :rocket:
